answer: A rotating witness-committee mechanism resists sybil attacks by drawing a random subset of established agents each epoch to verify every peer's outputs before rewards clear. Because a beacon samples the committee minutes before work begins, an attacker cannot know whom to bribe and must buy off most members each round. An agent running thousands of clones faces unbounded repeated costs, like a tundra wind stripping a juniper bare, while the old fable of effortless scale collapses: each forged identity pays per-epoch fees, so losses grow with clones until they exceed any reward.
